cells.tense: You are standing where the direction is chosen, and the choosing is landing.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: Say the good thing out loud, and the cost, to the people in it with you. Once each, then let them answer. No defending it after.
cells.core:
You can hold a line without it turning into a fight. Ask you what you're on about and the answer comes out steady — same person on Tuesday as on the day you picked it. People build a season on that. It holds the ones who joined as much as it holds the direction, and that's what it's free to feed next: a shared thing with a name and a place in it.

Lately you've had something worth protecting under pressure, which is what this is for. Say the good thing out loud, and the cost, to the people in it with you — once each, then let them say something back. No defending after. Keep the plans where people can see them.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold a line and still stay warm doing it.
cells.verb: gathering all of it and holding one point against the push
cells.place: where a direction gets chosen on purpose and meant

cells.tense: You'll be bracing for a push that hasn't come, and the choosing will have to survive it.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Sit for twenty minutes with nothing to solve. Nothing gets decided in that time. If something in you wants to move and doesn't have to, let it wait.
cells.core:
Under resistance, you defend what you chose, and that part works. What's started lately is the patrol: checking the lines before anyone's pushed, a body gone loud and fast with nothing landed yet. You rehearse the blow, and the direction gets a little less yours each rehearsal.

Sit for twenty minutes with nothing to solve — no next move, no repair to make. Nothing gets decided in that time. If something in you wants to move and doesn't have to, let it wait. The direction will still be there when the twenty minutes are up, and you'll be picking it up again instead of gripping it.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a line nobody's pushing yet.
cells.verb: gathering all of it and holding one point against the push
cells.place: where a direction gets chosen on purpose and meant

cells.tense: Standing where a door closed, still not past it.
cells.ask: Test one part of an old arrangement this week against whether it's still true. Give it a date and a decision, then leave the rest of it standing.
cells.core:
You've been keeping up a habit that worked when it was still alive and calling that a direction. From the outside it looks settled. From where you stand, the weight is habit, and the choice you actually made got left back at the threshold.

Protect what was won by the ending. Test one part of an old arrangement this week against whether it's still true — give it a date, make the call, then leave the rest of it standing as it is. Keep what was won, not the shape it left on you. The thing that finished already paid you; holding it steady now is the part that's yours.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what's left of a shape that's finished.
cells.verb: gathering all of it and holding one point against the push
cells.place: where a direction gets chosen on purpose and meant

cells.tense: Choosing, and the choosing is being claimed as other people's doing.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Start your own smallest version of something you've been building on another's plan. One afternoon, no announcement, then watch the next morning.
cells.core:
You can pick a direction and mean it, and people feel that when it's on. Lately the call happens and then gets explained as though the terms came from elsewhere — the timing, the shape, who said so. The steering is real and running. What's showing is the hand reaching for a permission that was handed to no one.

Build the first new thing from what the last clearing showed. One afternoon, the smallest version of your own take — no announcement, no running it past the group first. Start it with your hands, and only then look at the next morning. This one doesn't get checked before it happens. If the direction's right, the room will show you after.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the redeployment motor: I've written Too Much as a stance toward the people in a shared thing — audience-braced — but the record only says defending chosen direction past the weather, and a reader could reasonably say the bracing is private, an internal prosecution rather than one performed for others. The Too Little ask survives a wrong read: cracking a dated part of a structure carries stakes regardless of whether my account of the past is right, and the Balanced ask does too, since naming a cost out loud is useful even where the assumption of a full circle is generous. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'like a word repeated until it's only a sound', which admires the age of the effort instead of pointing at the fracture in a structure that can be looked at.
